statedAs.text: Les moyens à l’aide desquels la chasse d’un animal est permise sont: ... 5°  les balles qui ne sont pas traçantes et les balles autres que celles à pointe dure du type militaire et à bout non écrasant;

unresolved: STATE IS ALLOWED, DELIBERATELY NOT PROHIBITED. The regulation frames this as a list of permitted means whose members are bullets that are not tracer and not military hard-point non-expanding. Recording tracer or military hard-point ammunition as PROHIBITED would be the complement of a permitted list, which rule 4 forbids. If Québec states a prohibition elsewhere, it needs its own row from that source.

officialName.text: Les engins de chasse sont regroupés selon les types suivants

statedAs.text: 31. Les engins de chasse sont regroupés selon les types suivants: [types 1 à 14, définis par calibre, pression, diamètre de coupe et type de cartouche — texte intégral conservé dans engineTypes]

engineTypes.note: Verbatim definitions, reproduced because every method and ammunition answer for Québec resolves through them. Type 6 and type 11 are the two named by the hunter-orange exemption in r.1 s.17.3(1).
engineTypes.type5: les carabines utilisées avec des cartouches à percussion latérale de calibre .22
engineTypes.type6: les arcs ayant une pression d’au moins 18 kg à l’intérieur d’une extension de 0 à 71 cm et les flèches à tête d’acier ayant un diamètre de coupe d’au moins 22 mm
engineTypes.type8: l’épuisette, l’hameçon, l’assommoir, la fosse, la barrière, le dard ou la main
engineTypes.type11: a) les arcs ayant une pression d’au moins 18 kg à l’intérieur d’une extension de 0 à 71 cm et les flèches ayant un diamètre de coupe d’au moins 22 mm; b) les arbalètes ayant une pression d’au moins 54 kg et munies d’un cran de sûreté; le vireton doit avoir une longueur d’au moins 40 cm et la pointe doit avoir un diamètre de coupe d’au moins 22 mm
engineTypes.typesNotTranscribed: Types 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 12, 13 and 14 were read in full and are not transcribed here to keep this package to its scope. They are recoverable from the cited source at the recorded sha256.
engineTypes.identityCollision: TYPE 11 AND TYPE 12 SHARE THEIR ENTIRE BOW AND CROSSBOW DEFINITION, WORD FOR WORD. Type 11 is a) arcs + b) arbalètes. Type 12 is the same a) and b) plus c) fusils de calibre 10, 12, 16, 20 à balles ou projectiles ≥ 7,6 mm and d) fusils ou carabines à chargement par la bouche, canon unique, calibre ≥ 11 mm, une seule balle à la fois. Two types with different regulatory identity and an identical archery definition: an implement list of bow+crossbow cannot distinguish them, and provisions such as s.17(3) name exactly one.

unresolved: s.31 DEFINES the types. WHICH type applies to which species, zone and season segment is set by annexe III (and annexes IV, V, VI for particular territories), which was not read in this pass — seasons are the Canada lane's assignment. So this package establishes what each type IS, not when each is permitted.

The regulation names 14 types. Note that r.1 s.17.3(1) refers to 'un engin de type 6 ou 11'; both are archery types, which is why the big-game orange exemption is effectively an archery-season exemption. That relationship is stated here as an observation of the two texts, and is NOT a derived rule.

Un citoyen canadien qui est un résident au moment de sa demande peut obtenir un certificat du chasseur pour la chasse à l’aide d’une arme à feu sans remplir les conditions mentionnées aux paragraphes 4 et 5 du premier alinéa à la condition de présenter un certificat ou une preuve de compétence équivalente émise par une province ou un territoire canadien.

unresolved: THE CERTIFICATE IS WEAPON-CODED, so it interacts with method: s.5 gives code «F» chasse à l’aide d’une arme à feu, code «A» chasse à l’aide d’une arbalète ou d’un arc, code «P» piégeage. A hunter holding only «A» is not certified for a firearm season. The engine needs the code, not merely 'has a certificate'.

The snare exemption is SPECIES AND METHOD specific: it exempts the «Lièvre ou lapin à queue blanche au moyen de collet» licence, which touches snowshoe hare and eastern cottontail taken by collet (engin de type 7). It does not exempt those species taken by any other means.
s.5 says the certificate 'est valide tant que le titulaire est un résident'. It does not expire on a date; it lapses on ceasing to be a resident. That is not a licence-year concept.

The «Lièvre ou lapin à queue blanche au moyen de collet» licence is method-bound to the collet, which s.31(7) defines as «engin de type 7». The certificate exemption therefore attaches to an engin type, not merely to a word.

The accompanying holder's certificate must match 'l’engin de chasse qu’il utilise' — the weapon the exempt hunter is using, not the companion's own preference.
'une seule fois dans sa vie' is a lifetime-scoped condition North Ground cannot verify and must never assert as satisfied.

unresolved: A COUPON COUNT IS NOT A BAG LIMIT, and the two disagree on purpose. Black bear is issued 2 coupons and s.26 caps the year at 2 but distributes them by zone and season so that some zones allow only 1. Spring turkey is issued 2 coupons while s.27.1 caps the year at 3 across two segments. Use the LIMIT rows for limits and this row only for what is issued.
«Ours noir valide pour la zone 13» and «zone 16» are listed for 'ii. non-résident' only, with 0 coupons. Recorded as stated; why they differ is not explained by the table.

statedAs.text: Sous réserve du deuxième alinéa, tout permis de chasse expire à la fin de la période de chasse à l’animal ou au groupe d’animaux pour lequel il est délivré ou lorsque l’animal a été identifié à l’aide d’un coupon de transport ou aurait dû l’être conformément au Règlement sur les activités de chasse (chapitre C-61.1, r. 1) ou, dans le cas des permis de cerf sans bois ou de l’orignal sans bois, lorsqu’une personne qui utilise ce permis tue un animal pour lequel il est délivré.
Malgré le premier alinéa, le permis de chasse au petit gibier est valide de sa date de délivrance jusqu’à la date d’expiration qui y est inscrite.
Tout permis remplacé, conformément à l’article 12, expire à la date de délivrance du nouveau permis.

unresolved: A Québec hunting licence is NOT a licence-year artefact for most species: it expires when the season ends OR when an animal is tagged, whichever comes first. The small-game licence is the exception and runs to a printed date. Any fee or validity model keyed on a licence year will be wrong for big game.
'ou aurait dû l’être' means the licence can expire on a tagging that should have happened. North Ground cannot observe that and must never assert a licence is still valid.

unresolved: s.17 OVERRIDES THE SEASON TABLES. Sections 14, 15 and 25 each open 'Sous réserve de l’article 17', so a season in annexe III does not authorise an antlerless moose hunt unless s.17 also permits it. An engine reading the season annexe alone gets this wrong.
PARAGRAPH 2 IS YEAR-SPECIFIC: zones 13, 18 and 28 are permitted 'au cours de l’année 2027' only. A date-blind reading makes it permanent. Carried verbatim; the year is not generalised.
Paragraph 3 turns on 'un engin de type 11' — defined in s.31 and carried in the engine-types row.
The composition value NARROWS is taken from the authority's own 'Sous réserve de l’article 17' in s.14, not inferred from specificity.

ENGIN TYPE IS THE AUTHORITY'S DECISIVE UNIT HERE AND AN IMPLEMENT LIST CANNOT CARRY IT. s.31 defines type 11 and type 12 with IDENTICAL bow and crossbow paragraphs, word for word; type 12 adds shotgun slugs and muzzleloaders. So a bow-and-crossbow implement list is ambiguous between types 11 and 12, and s.17(3) names exactly one. Verified against s.31 in this same source.

absenceEvidence.finding: 'lièvre arctique' appears exactly ONCE in the whole regulation, in the s.2 definition of «petit gibier». It appears nowhere in SECTION IV LIMITES DE CAPTURE. This source states no bag limit for arctic hare.
absenceEvidence.closedBy: NOT CLOSED. This is a statement about this instrument, not about Québec law. A limit may sit in another regulation, in a territory-specific annexe, or in the small-game guide. Recorded as unresolved, NOT as NOT_APPLICABLE and NOT as 'no limit applies'.
absenceEvidence.instrumentNote: Instrument named in full in `instruments`; no bare section numbers are used in this record.

schemaGapsReported: PERIOD 'par séjour' (s.24(2), zone 20 deer): the authority's period is per STAY, which is none of DAY | SEASON | LICENCE_YEAR. Recorded as SEASON with a periodNote saying it is not the source's word.

PER-GROUP LIMITS (s.25): '1 orignal, par 2 chasseurs, par année' and '1 orignal, par 3 chasseurs' divide the limit across hunters. value.count carries no divisor, so a naive read is 2x-3x too permissive.
PERIODLESS STANDING CAP (companion package, r.1 s.18): a possession cap with no period stated at all, where period is required and has no default.

OBSERVATION, not yet a gap: an AUTHORIZATION whose validity ends on an EVENT (tagging an animal) rather than a date — s.11. `obtain`/`requires` carry prerequisites but nothing carries event-based expiry. Flagged before it becomes a wrong date.

ENGIN TYPE HAS NO STRUCTURED HOME. The authority's decisive unit for method is «engin de type N», referenced throughout r.12 — s.17(3), s.34.1, annexe III — and by r.1 s.17.3(1) for the orange exemption. The schema's scope.methods is a string list, which cannot carry it: s.31 defines types 11 and 12 with identical bow/crossbow paragraphs, so 'bow, crossbow' is ambiguous between two types that the law treats differently. I have added a non-schema scope.enginTypes field on the affected rows rather than flattening; it needs a real home or a ruling to drop it.
